name: Galleriq
author: Shakil Khan

sections.description:
Galleriq lets you create a separate image gallery for every project, portfolio item, or client, and manage everything from the WordPress dashboard.

Each gallery has its own set of images (upload and reorder by drag and drop) and its own slider settings: width mode (boxed, wide, or full screen), height, image fit, colors, autoplay, and whether arrows, thumbnails, and side slides are shown.

Once a gallery is created, place its shortcode in any page or post to display an interactive, touch-friendly slider.

Features

  • Unlimited galleries, one per project
  • Drag-and-drop image reordering
  • Width control: boxed, wide, or full screen
  • Custom colors, corner radius, and padding
  • Autoplay with adjustable delay
  • Arrows with three modes: always show, show on hover, or hide
  • Thumbnail strip with custom background color and size
  • Touch swipe and keyboard navigation
  • Responsive, with a separate height setting for mobile
sections.installation:
1. Upload the galleriq folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Galleriq → Add New, upload images, and adjust the gallery settings.
  4. Copy the shortcode shown for that gallery (for example [galleriq id="123"]) and paste it into any page or post.
sections.faq:
Can I have different settings for each gallery?

Yes. Every gallery has its own independent settings for width, height, colors, autoplay, and arrows.

Can I hide the arrows or thumbnails?

Yes. Both can be turned off in the Gallery Settings box on each gallery’s edit screen. Arrows also support a “show on hover” mode. You can also override the arrows per placement, for example [galleriq id="123" arrows="hide"].

Does it work on mobile?

Yes. Galleries are touch-swipeable and have a separate height setting for mobile screens.

I used an earlier version. Will my galleries still work?

Yes. Existing galleries are migrated automatically when you open the WordPress dashboard, and the old [project_gallery] shortcode keeps working.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Coding standards: scripts and styles are now loaded through the WordPress enqueue system.
  • Security: all input is unslashed and sanitized, nonces are verified correctly, and all output is escaped.
  • Renamed internal prefixes to galleriq_ and added automatic migration of existing galleries.
  • New primary shortcode [galleriq id="123"] (the old [project_gallery] shortcode still works).

1.1.0

  • Added width control (boxed / wide / full screen)
  • Added arrow display modes (always / hover / hide) with size and color settings
  • Added thumbnail strip background color and size settings
  • Added autoplay, colors, padding, and corner radius settings

1.0.0

  • Initial release
